text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen 1.2% today and nearly 18% over two weeks, with the sharpest drops occurring right after the midterm elections. The core driver appears to be political: a Democratic sweep signals reduced support for fossil fuels and increased momentum toward renewable energy, which directly threatens demand for refined oil products and refinery margins. While U.S. oil prices remain stable at $99.64 per barrel, that stability masks the longer-term concern that a Democratic Congress will prioritize wind and solar over traditional energy.

The timing underscores the shift—the stock began its steepest decline on November 4th, the day after election results became clear. Refineries are still running near capacity at 94.5%, but that operating strength can't offset the market's forward-looking fear that policy will eventually shrink fuel demand. For a refiner, the risk isn't today's oil prices or current production levels; it's the trajectory of demand five to ten years out under a government now openly hostile to fossil fuel expansion.
